thread.title: Congressional leaders respond after NTSB meeting on DCA midair collision
thread.title_full: Congressional leaders respond after NTSB meeting on DCA midair collision

author: L. L. Dube
title: Congressional leaders respond after NTSB meeting on DCA midair collision
text:
On January 27, 2026, leaders from the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee released a joint statement following a National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) board meeting. The meeting addressed the midair collision that took place on January 29, 2025, at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport between American Airlines Flight 5342 and a UH-60 Army Black Hawk helicopter.
The statement was issued by Committee Chairman Sam Graves (R-MO), Ranking Member Rick Larsen (D-WA), Aviation Subcommittee Chairman Troy E. Nehls (R-TX), and Aviation Subcommittee Ranking Member André Carson (D-IN). They expressed their ongoing condolences to the families affected by the incident: “As we approach the anniversary of the tragic DCA mid-air collision, our thoughts and condolences remain with the families of the victims. We greatly appreciate the work of the NTSB, and now that they have met to finalize their findings and recommendations, we will review those along with the agency’s final report as we work to address the issues raised and determine the Committee’s next oversight and legislative steps. We remain committed to protecting travelers and making the U.S. airspace as safe as possible.”
The NTSB’s investigation aimed to determine causes of such accidents and offer recommendations for improving aviation safety in U.S. airspace.
